thread:
incident-bot: paging -> HIGH: multiple customers reporting 502/504s from inference gateway in private VPC (us-west-2). Error surge started ~1765432090. Escalating to oncall. INC-4821

alice: acked, I'm oncall. verifying scope. which customers? any public endpoints ok?

carla: seeing elevated 5xx on gateway logs for private subnets only. public-hosted models unaffected. sample log: `upstream connect error or disconnect while reading response header from upstream`, lots of `504 gateway timeout`.

alice: running quick check: `curl -v https://inference-gw-private.us-west-2.redwood/api/health` -> hangs then `504`.

ben: I see high NAT ephemeral port usage on the private NAT appliance for that VPC. metrics: ephemeral ports in use ~ 58k of 64k. conntrack entries spiked. possible SNAT exhaustion.

derek: confirming, cloud NAT metrics show `ActiveConnections` spike and `ConnectionErrors` increasing. peering path shows retransmits.

alice: tagging networking. ben, can you pull conntrack counts on the NAT nodes + check security groups?

ben: on it. `ssh nat-prod-03` -> `sudo conntrack -S` shows total=120000, hashsize=16384, entries=62000 -> nearing nf_conntrack_max 65536. Also saw `iptables -L -n` no weird DROP rules. SGs look fine but I saw a recent rollout that tightened ephemeral ports on a customer-facing SG? investigating.

carla: from gateway side: worker pods show a lot of `ECONNRESET` upstream, and the runtime logs show retries then 502. kubectl logs show `open() failed: Too many open files` for the gateway process on a couple nodes. might be cascading from failed upstream connections.

alice: immediate mitigation idea: fail traffic for affected private subnets to secondary NAT (standby) and increase conntrack max. can we patch kernel param and swap route? minimal blast radius first.

ben: I can increase conntrack on the NAT instances now: `sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=2000000` and persist to /etc/sysctl.d/99-nf.conf. doing that on nat-prod-0[1-3] now.

derek: I'm preparing a route table change to point the subnet's default route to the standby NAT in the same AZ. will apply to one subnet as canary and monitor.

carla: also going to cordon+drain the two gateway nodes hitting fd limits and restart the inference-gateway service after bumping `ulimit -n` to 100k on the systemd unit. prepping PR for systemd drop-in.

alice: good. Ben, confirm conntrack bump applied?

ben: done on nat-prod-01/02/03. conntrack_max now 2M. entries dropping as old connections age. ephemeral usage still high but reclaiming.

derek: route table change applied to subnet-abc (canary). traffic for that subnet now goes to nat-standby-az1. monitor logs/metrics.

carla: canary looks healthy: 502 rate down from 18% -> 1.2% for that subnet. node restarts finished, workers back to normal, no more `Too many open files`.

alice: rolling to other subnets in small batches. status: applying route change to subnet-def next.

status-bot: Incident INC-4821 status page updated -> "Degraded: Private inference gateway experiencing elevated 5xx/timeouts for some customers in us-west-2. Mitigation in progress."

ben: root cause I'm seeing so far: a recent customer peering config rollout reduced allowed ephemeral port range on a security group attached to a transit peering appliance. Combined with longer-lived connections and a NAT conntrack spike, SNAT entries exhausted and connections started failing, causing gateway retries and FD exhaustion on edge nodes.

carla: good catch. can someone revert the SG change for the peering appliance? if we open ephemeral range 32768-61000 and allow established connections we should see normal behavior.

alice: on it, contacting infra owner. I'm going to open a temporary SG rule to allow 32768-61000 from the peering CIDR on transit-eni. performed now.

ben: after SG change, ephemeral reclaim accelerated, connection errors dropping. `netstat -an | grep TIME_WAIT | wc -l` down 40%. gateway 5xx rate now ~0.4% cluster-wide.

derek: rolling to remaining subnets done. monitoring 15m.

alice: customer impact: 12 private customers in us-west-2 had degraded requests between 1765432090-1765432145. we escalated to P1 internally due to SLO breach risk. ops: some customers saw transient 502/504s and increased latency. support notified and CS drafting targeted email.

carla: postmortem actions captured: (1) revert/validate peering SG rollout process; (2) add automated gate in rollout to detect ephemeral range shrink; (3) add conntrack alert threshold earlier; (4) ensure `ulimit` bump and systemd drop-in deployed to gateway AMIs; (5) add fallback routing automation to move to standby NAT for SNAT pressure.

alice: handing off to carla for follow-ups and postmortem. I'll stay available for 30m then clear oncall. carla, please confirm next steps and timeline.

carla: taking over. I'll own the postmortem, timeline for deliverable: initial draft in 48h. will coordinate with networking and infra to schedule fix rollouts.

alice: thanks everyone. incident-bot, mark incident as mitigated but still monitoring.

incident-bot: INC-4821 status -> Mitigated. Monitoring.

carla: leaving notes in the runbook: commands run, SG rule id added, conntrack sysctl value, route table changes, affected customer list. will link ticket when draft ready.

alice: closing oncall handoff now. if anything regresses ping me. :thumbsup:
